question: Why is the term 'aloneness' used despite non-difference from Śiva?
premises: Prior impressions may still give rise to suspicion of difference.
The text now speaks of aloneness.
Alternatively, the term may be used from another standpoint.
inference: The term 'aloneness' is used provisionally, either because old impressions of difference persist or because of another standpoint.
uncertainties: The phrase 'another measure' (mātrāntara) is somewhat ambiguous in this context.
plain_english: Even so, because suspicion based on old impressions of difference may persist, the text now speaks of aloneness; or else it does so from another standpoint.
